REASON FOR REFERRAL: Diagnostic test for Nucleotide Excision Repair Disorder (Xeroderma Pigmentosum group C (XP-C))
Patient is affected with XP-C, testing has been requested to identify the causative variants in the XPC gene.

TEST
Screen for pathogenic sequence variants in the XPC gene by fluorescent bi-directional Sanger sequencing.  Variants confirmed by fluorescent bi-directional Sanger sequencing using new DNA dilution.

RESULTS
Heterozygous XPC c.362delA p.(Asp121fs) variant detected
Heterozygous XPC c.445_446delGA p.(Glu149fs) variants detected

SUMMARY 
Both the XPC c.362delA p.(Asp121fs) and XPC c.445_446delGA p.(Glu149fs) sequence variants are predicted to be pathogenic1.  Pathogenic variants in this gene are associated with the Nucleotide Excision Repair Disorder XP-C.  Assuming these variants are in trans, this result confirms a clinical diagnosis of XP-C.

FURTHER WORK
This individual?s parents should be tested for the presence of these sequence variants in order to confirm that they are in trans. 
Once their carrier status has been determined accurate prenatal diagnosis can be offered to Patient?s parents if required.
If appropriate, other adult members of this family can be offered carrier testing. We recommend that they are referred to Clinical Genetics for counselling prior to molecular testing.

Notes
Exons 1-16 of the XPC gene and adjacent splice sites were screened for variants by fluorescent Sanger sequencing.
1Assessment of pathogenicity is carried out using bioinformatics software Alamut.
Variant nomenclature based on XPC gene reference sequence LRG_472, with nucleotide number 1 corresponding to the first base of the translation initiation codon.
